corrects_my_own_claim.i_said: "a real second process contends for the PRODUCTION lock <WORK>/sandbox.lock"
corrects_my_own_claim.what_is_true: that is the lock `lab_data` and `lab_containment` take, and the fixture is valid evidence for it. It is NOT the lock an episode worker takes: the worker uses a DIFFERENT CLASS (lab_worker.ExecutionLock) on a DIFFERENT FILE (<WORK>/<trial>/sandbox.lock). Saying "the production lock" implied a single lock, and there is more than one.
corrects_my_own_claim.what_the_fixture_still_shows: exclusion on the reference-sweep/containment lock, with its controls. Nothing in it is withdrawn; its SCOPE is narrower than my sentence implied.

finding.covered: the two workers WITHIN a trial: they share the trial lock, which is the case 5.7 is titled for
finding.decision_is_roots: pointing every path at one host-wide lock file changes a production lock path, which is a protocol-conformance change. It is not made here.
finding.has_it_bitten: NO. 0 trial episodes and 0 calibration episodes have ever run, so nothing has been corrupted. This is latent, not manifested.

a reference sweep and an episode worker -- different lock files
finding.what: production resolves 5 distinct lock files, not one
finding.why_it_matters: the shared writable sandbox base is /private/tmp/labsbx/ls_sbx for EVERY run on the host regardless of trial, and during verification it holds hidden tests and the nonce sentinel in clear text. A lock that is not host-wide does not exclude the reader 5.7 names.

paths.two_workers_share_reason: both workers of a trial receive the SAME ctx.paths.sandbox_lock from the orchestrator, so the intra-trial case protocol 5.7 is titled for IS covered

protocol_requirement: protocol 5.7 item 1: an exclusive flock on ONE LOCK FILE; "at most one generated program exists and runs at any instant". The hazard it addresses is a Seatbelt writable directory SHARED BY EVERY RUN ON THE HOST, so the property is host-wide, not per-trial.
